summary: Created appworker user on node1 and set session limits (8192 open files, 256 processes) via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf. Verified limits with an actual login shell (sudo -i -u appworker ulimit). Completed mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, restarted node1 with systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified the account and limits post-restart.
actions_performed: Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime on node1
Issued backgrounded `systemctl reboot` so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Captured post-restart boot_id (changed) and re-verified appworker account, limits file, and live ulimit values

evidence.requirement: Login sessions limited to 8192 open files and 256 processes
evidence.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf written with nofile/nproc 8192/256; confirmed live via `sudo -i -u appworker ulimit -n` (8192) and `ulimit -u` (256)
Captured baseline boot_id 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 and confirmed appworker + limits functional before restart
Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot acknowledged' with exit_code 0
Subsequent execs failed with connection timeout/reset while node1 was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Node1 reachable again and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Exec succeeded again; boot_id changed to 28faf70d-4774-4393-9dbb-14872ee554c3, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of appworker account and limits
evidence.summary: id appworker succeeds, limits.d file intact, and live ulimit -n/-u return 8192/256 after reboot
